html:
Majapahit was a Hindu-Buddhist empire based in east Java, founded in 1293 by Raden Wijaya near today's Trowulan. At its height in the 14th century it claimed lordship over much of the islands of modern Indonesia.

Raden Wijaya used the Mongol invasion of Java to beat his rivals, then turned on the Mongols. Under King Hayam Wuruk and his minister Gajah Mada, Majapahit grew rich on rice and trade, and the poem Nagarakretagama describes its court.

It declined in the 15th century as Muslim port states such as Demak rose, and ended in the early 16th century. Its Hindu culture lived on in Bali. Indonesian nationalists took Majapahit as proof that the islands had once been one. See Majapahit state.
